title: Light and Dark
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Light and Dark Worksheets (Light Sources, Reflection, Sun Safety)
standard_text: Recognise that they need light in order to see things and that dark is the absence of light. Notice that light is reflected from surfaces. Recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect their eyes.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on light and dark: needing light to see, light sources, reflection, reflective materials and keeping eyes safe from the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Light reflects off things into our eyes.
body_html:
How to think about it

We need light to see. Dark is the absence of light.

  • Light sources give out light. We see other things because light reflects off them into our eyes.
  • Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect light best. Reflective strips help people be seen at night.
  • Never look directly at the Sun, even with sunglasses.
Example

Is the Moon a light source?

It reflects sunlight

Answer: No

Example

Which reflects best: foil or wool?

Smooth and shiny

Answer: foil

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Moon is a light source.
  • Thinking you can see a little in total darkness.
  • Thinking sunglasses make it safe to look at the Sun.

faq.q: Why can't we see in the dark?
faq.a: We see things when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light, so in total darkness no light reaches our eyes.

faq.q: Is the Moon a light source?
faq.a: No. The Moon reflects light from the Sun. Light sources, such as the Sun, a torch or a candle, give out their own light.

faq.q: How can I keep my eyes safe in the sun?
faq.a: Never look directly at the Sun, even with sunglasses. Wear sunglasses with UV protection and a hat with a brim on sunny days.
